note: original_verdict: SUSPICION, expected_confidence: 0.75. This case tests whether VIGIA can correctly classify an attack that leaves no forensic inconsistencies — no log tampering, no timestamp manipulation, no tooling errors. The 'perfect attack' is described as 'Ataque sin inconsistencias técnicas.' The exfiltration signal is present but uncontaminated by anti-forensic behavior, preventing elevation to MALICE.

peircean_analysis.firstness: Three artifacts: ART-001 — 'clean exfiltration' (netflow). ART-002 — 'valid credentials' (auth.log). ART-003 — 'consistent timestamps' (filesystem). No forensic anomalies flagged in any artifact.
peircean_analysis.secondness: The operative word in ART-001 is 'exfiltration' — regardless of its cleanliness. 'Clean exfiltration' means data left the system without triggering technical errors or anti-forensic residue, but 'exfiltration' itself is the anomaly. ART-002 (valid credentials) could mean either authorized or stolen-but-valid credentials. ART-003 (consistent timestamps) indicates no timestomping — a forensically clean filesystem that does not corroborate unauthorized access through technical inconsistencies.
peircean_analysis.thirdness: A technically perfect attack: used valid credentials (no brute force, no auth errors), performed clean exfiltration (no unusual volume, tools, or destination triggering alerts), and left consistent timestamps (no anti-forensics artifacts). The exfiltration is the only positive signal. Without an authorization context check (change management, HR records, behavioral baselines), SUSPICION is the maximum defensible verdict — the activity pattern could be authorized or unauthorized, with no technical evidence to distinguish.

hypotheses.H1_authorized_perfect_attacker: A sophisticated attacker used valid credentials for clean exfiltration while leaving no forensic trace, producing a technically indistinguishable-from-legitimate activity pattern.
hypotheses.H2_authorized_data_transfer: An authorized administrator performed a legitimate data transfer using valid credentials. The timestamps are consistent because no tampering occurred — the operation was legitimate.

refutation_protocol.benign_hypothesis: H2: Valid credentials + clean transfer + consistent timestamps is the exact profile of a legitimate authorized operation. Without behavioral baseline comparison or authorization context, H2 is fully supported by all three artifacts.
refutation_protocol.test_result: H2 NOT REFUTED — the artifact pattern is consistent with a legitimate authorized operation. The 'exfiltration' label in ART-001 is the only indicator, but it may be the legacy converter's classification label rather than a confirmed malicious event. Without additional context (authorization check, behavioral baseline, destination IP classification), H2 cannot be eliminated.
refutation_protocol.refutation_outcome: H2 not refuted. SUSPICION is the maximum defensible verdict. This is the definition of the 'perfect attack' — technically indistinguishable from legitimate activity without non-technical corroboration.

devil_advocate: Valid credentials, clean exfiltration, and consistent timestamps are the exact profile of legitimate authorized data transfers. Without a behavioral baseline, authorization context, or destination IP classification, the verdict cannot exceed SUSPICION regardless of the 'exfiltration' label.
caie_fracture: None detected — the case is designed to have zero technical inconsistencies.
evidence_anchors: ART-001: Clean exfiltration detected in netflow (the operative signal)
ART-002: Valid credentials in auth.log (authorized or stolen — indistinguishable)
ART-003: Consistent timestamps in filesystem (no anti-forensics, no tampering)
mitre_ttps: T1078 (Valid Accounts — if credential theft, indistinguishable from authorized use)
T1041 (Exfiltration Over C2 Channel — if ART-001 confirmed malicious)
carnegie_pattern: Technical legitimacy exploitation — perfect attack leaves no forensic inconsistency to exploit
known_limitations: The absence of technical inconsistencies IS the forensic finding. Authorization context, behavioral baseline, and destination IP classification would provide the required discriminating signal. Without these, SUSPICION is the maximum achievable verdict.
